name: Jeru the Damaja

sources: style-research-extended vol.1 boom-bap — Jeru the Damaja

Wikipedia — The Sun Rises in the East
notes: 100% Premier production, and the research describes the emptiest version of it: "1- or 2-bar loops, static tonic drones; the 'chord' is often a single stab. Extremely low note density." So `melody.densityPerBar` tops out at 3, `chordToneBias` is deliberately low, and `halfStepDissonance` is the second-highest on this axis after Mobb Deep — the research names "deliberately clashing intervals (minor 2nd/tritone)" as the identifying feature, and a minor 2nd against the tonic is exactly what that parameter emits. The kick sits on 1 and the 4th 8th, so `secondaryAnchor` is `2&` rather than the axis's usual `3&`. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set and it is a description rather than an exemption — the harmony is one stab. Its variety therefore comes from `chordDurationBeats` and three `harmonicRhythm` values rather than from progressions it does not play. ⚠ The `i–iv` family is INFERRED, not researched: the research names only static tonic drones. It carries the lowest weight and exists because the generated chord part still owes a producer 55 distinct outputs over 200 seeds and the bass needs more than one reachable root; it is the first thing to delete if this model ever sounds busier than the records do. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick`, not one held note, and that is an engine limit rather than a reading of the record.** The research says filtered sample bass, one note per bar. `reese_sustain` is the only rhythm that holds a note and it saturates, so `mirror_kick` over a kick that plays 1 and 2& with `followRootsProb` 0.94 is the nearest honest thing. ⚠ `phraseBars` reaches 4 as well as 1 and 2, weighted 1:4:2 so the short loop the research describes still dominates — one loop length bounds every derived part, and the 4 is INFERRED headroom rather than a claim about the records. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates this high-medium; the documented half is Premier's method, and the artist-side tempo band is catalog-level. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 942 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [2,1,4], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
